answer: In PoA, each bonded identity is independently slashable, but correlated equivocation—shared timing, conflicting votes, funding, or control proofs—aggregates across k identities, imposing a quadratic O(k^2) penalty rather than k linear fines. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the coordinated swarm, rapidly exhausting escrow and making sybil expansion uneconomic; a relic cannot bridge accountability, and every terrace of aliases remains exposed.
